# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XIX. POOR ADAM!

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Upon Ida’s arrival at the house, Grace remained face down across her mattress, completely declining any solace. Adam had been slain by Aunt Martha. At that exact moment, he lay upon a plate inside the pantry, bound and prepared for cooking, surrounded by his own gizzard, heart, and liver. Aunt Martha paid not the slightest attention to Grace’s overwhelming fury and sorrow.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0000 }

“We needed to provide a meal for the unusual minister,” she stated. “You are far too grown-up to cause such a commotion about an aged rooster. You were aware that he would need to be slaughtered eventually.”
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0001 }

“When father gets back, I’m going to inform him of what you did,” Grace said through her tears.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0002 }

“Do not go disturbing your unfortunate father, as his worries are already sufficient, and I serve as the housekeeper in this place.”
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0003 }

“Adam belonged to me—Mrs. Johnson presented him to me. You possessed no right to lay a finger on him,” Grace declared furiously.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0004 }

“Refrain from being impudent now. The rooster has been slaughtered, concluding the matter. I refuse to serve an unfamiliar clergyman a meal consisting of cold boiled mutton. My upbringing taught me greater propriety than that, despite my reduced circumstances.”
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0005 }

Grace refused to head downstairs for supper on that evening, nor would she attend church on the following morning. Nevertheless, when dinner time arrived, she took her seat at the table, possessing puffy eyes from weeping and a moody expression.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0006 }

Possessing a gleaming bald pate, thick white eyebrows, and a stubbly white moustache, the Rev. James Perry was a smooth, ruddy-faced man. Although he was undeniably unattractive and a most tedious, self-important individual, Grace would have harbored the exact same deep hatred for him even had his appearance matched the Archangel Michael and his speech possessed the eloquence of men and angels. Displaying his well-formed diamond ring and fleshy white hands, he skillfully sliced Adam into pieces. Furthermore, he offered cheerful observations throughout the entire process. While Tobias and Rupert chuckled, even Ida produced a faint smile, believing good manners required such a response. Grace, however, merely wore a deep frown. Her behavior struck the Rev. James as terribly rude. On one occasion, as he was making a self-righteous comment to Tobias, Grace abruptly interrupted him with a direct denial. The Rev. James knitted his thick eyebrows together as he looked at her.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0007 }

“Young females must not interject,” he stated, “and it is improper for them to gainsay individuals possessing vastly superior knowledge to their own.”
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0008 }

This made Grace even more ill-tempered. Being addressed as “little girl” as though her size were no greater than plump Tessa Carrow’s over at Hollowmere! The indignity was unbearable. Furthermore, the way that dreadful Mr. Perry devoured his food! He went so far as to strip poor Adam’s bones bare. Grace and Ida both refused to consume a single bite, viewing the boys as barely distinguishable from cannibals. Grace believed that if the terrible meal did not finish shortly, she would terminate it herself by launching an object at Mr. Perry’s shiny head. Luckily, Mr. Perry discovered that Aunt Martha’s tough apple pie exceeded even his own chewing abilities, bringing the dinner to a close following an extended grace wherein Mr. Perry expressed pious gratitude for the sustenance and moderate delight provided by a benevolent and charitable Providence.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0009 }

“Grace, under her breath, muttered rebelliously that God had not had anything at all to do with supplying Adam for you.”
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0010 }

The boys were happy to flee outside, Ida departed to assist Aunt Martha with the washing-up—even if that quite crabby old woman never appreciated her hesitant help—and Grace went into the study, in whose grate a bright wood fire burned. Her belief was that this would allow her to get away from the despised Mr. Perry, who had declared that he planned to sleep in his room for the afternoon. Grace had hardly made herself comfortable in a corner with a book, however, when he entered and, positioning himself in front of the fire, began to examine the untidy study with an expression of displeasure.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0011 }

“Your father’s volumes appear to be in rather terrible disorder, my child,” he remarked sternly.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0012 }

Lurking in her corner, Grace grew somber and remained completely silent. She refused to speak with this—this creature.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0013 }

“Attempts ought to be made by you to arrange them,” Mr. Perry continued, fiddling with his attractive watch chain while offering a patronizing smile to Grace. “Your age is sufficient for you to manage tasks of this nature. A mere ten years old, my young daughter residing at home serves as an outstanding little housekeeper currently, offering her mother supreme assistance and solace. A truly sweet child describes her. The privilege of knowing her is something I wish was yours. Assistance could be provided to you by her in numerous manners. Unquestionably, the priceless benefit of being cared for and trained by a good mother has been denied to you. A sorrowful deficiency—a most sorrowful deficiency. On multiple occasions, I have conversed with your father regarding this matter, dutifully highlighting his obligation to him, yet up to now it has yielded no result. May he come to realize his obligation prior to the arrival of too late a moment, I hope. Currently, striving to fill the void left by your holy mother stands as your obligation and honor. A profound impact could be made by you upon your brothers and your young sister—a genuine mother to them is what you could become. A concern exists for me that these matters are not pondered by you as they ought to be. My dear child, permit me to enlighten your perception concerning them.”
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0014 }

Mr. Perry’s greasy, self-satisfied tone continued to flow. He felt completely in his element. To dictate, condescend, and urge others on was what suited him above all else. Having no intention of ceasing, he kept right on talking. Planted securely on the rug in front of the hearth, he emitted a torrent of grandiloquent truisms. Grace failed to catch a single word. In truth, she was paying him no attention whatsoever. She was, however, observing his lengthy black coat-tails, an amused mischief mounting in her brown eyes. Mr. Perry had positioned himself extremely close to the flames. His coat-tails started to singe—his coat-tails started to emit smoke. Enraptured by his own rhetoric, he persisted in his tedious speech. The smoke from the coat-tails grew thicker. A minuscule spark leaped from the ignited timber and landed right in the center of one tail. It attached itself, took hold, and expanded into a slow-burning fire. Unable to hold back any further, Grace burst into a suppressed laugh.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0015 }

Mr. Perry halted abruptly, enraged by such impudence. All at once, he realized that the chamber was filled with the smell of scorched fabric. Turning rapidly, he perceived nothing. After that, he slapped his hands onto his coat-tails, hauling them forward. A considerable tear had already formed in one tail—and he was wearing his new suit. Grace trembled, unable to control her laughter at his posture and face.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0016 }

“Was my coat-tail catching fire visible to you?” he inquired in a rage.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0017 }

“Yes, sir,” Grace replied with a modest air.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0018 }

“Why wasn’t I told?” he asked, staring at her with anger.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0019 }

“You mentioned that interrupting was not good manners, sir,” Grace said, with even greater demureness.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0020 }

“If—if I was your father, I would give you a spanking that you would remember all your life, Miss,” stated an exceedingly irate reverend gentleman, while he marched out of the study. Because the coat belonging to Mr. Ashdown’s second best suit proved the wrong size for Mr. Perry, he was forced to attend the evening service wearing his scorched coat-tail. However, he failed to process up the aisle possessing his accustomed awareness of the dignity he bestowed upon the edifice. He refused to ever consent to a pulpit swap with Mr. Ashdown in the future, and he proved scarcely polite to the gentleman when their paths crossed briefly at the station the following morning. Nevertheless, Grace experienced a degree of somber gratification. Adam had been avenged in part.
{: #nw-v05-c19-p0021 }
